assumptions.name: FY2026E Group revenue
assumptions.rationale: Base = midpoint of Grab's raised guidance range ($4.10-4.15bn) issued at Q2 2026. Bear = low end of prior (pre-raise) guidance, reflecting a competitive or macro shock in H2 2026. Bull = high end of raised guidance plus modest SuperBank/Stash upside.

assumptions.name: FY2026E Group Adjusted EBITDA
assumptions.rationale: Base = midpoint of raised guidance ($720-740m). Bear assumes a Deliveries margin setback (renewed competition) partially offset by Mobility resilience. Bull = top of guidance with continued advertising-led Deliveries upside.

assumptions.name: FY2027E Group revenue growth
assumptions.rationale: Deceleration from FY2026's ~22% guided growth toward a still-above-market rate; bear reflects Deliveries share loss to a well-funded Foodpanda/ShopeeFood combination; bull reflects continued share gains plus GoTo-related market consolidation.

assumptions.name: FY2028E Group revenue growth
assumptions.rationale: Consistent with management's disclosed '2025-2028 20% CAGR' guidance implying deceleration in later years off a larger base; bear/bull bracket competitive-intensity outcomes.

assumptions.name: FY2028E Group Adjusted EBITDA
assumptions.rationale: Base = management's own disclosed 2028 target, taken at face value as the base case given the company's 18-quarter track record of guidance credibility. Bear = Maybank's aggressive-competition scenario impact concentrated in Deliveries (~-$300-400m vs base) plus a still-loss-making Financial Services. Bull = target modestly exceeded on Deliveries margin upside and Financial Services reaching breakeven.

assumptions.name: Deliveries Segment Adjusted EBITDA margin (% of GMV), FY2028E
assumptions.rationale: FY2025 actual was 2.0%, Q2 2026 actual 2.3%; base case assumes continued gradual advertising-led expansion; bear assumes reversion below FY2025 levels on renewed price competition (Maybank's aggressive scenario implies up to -41% vs base 2030 EBITDA); bull assumes advertising penetration continues compounding with limited competitive response.

assumptions.name: Mobility Segment Adjusted EBITDA margin (% of GMV), FY2028E
assumptions.rationale: FY2025 actual 8.7%, Q2 2026 actual 8.6% (fuel-cost affected). Mobility is judged structurally less contested than Deliveries (higher barriers, license/regulatory moats in several markets), so the base/bear/bull range is narrower than Deliveries.

assumptions.name: Financial Services Segment Adjusted EBITDA, FY2028E
assumptions.rationale: FY2025 actual -$110m. Base assumes gradual narrowing as the loan book (currently +120-197% YoY growth) seasons and credit-loss provisioning normalizes as a percentage of the book. Bear assumes continued aggressive book growth keeps provisioning elevated, compounded by any regional credit-cycle deterioration (RISK-04). Bull assumes the segment crosses to breakeven/modest profit as NIM scales ahead of provisioning.

assumptions.name: Adjusted Free Cash Flow conversion (% of Adjusted EBITDA), FY2028E
assumptions.rationale: FY2025 actual 58% ($290m/$500m). Base tracks close to but slightly below management's explicit 80% 2028 target to reflect execution risk; bear assumes capex intensity or working-capital drag (e.g., loan-book funding needs) keeps conversion well below target; bull assumes the 80% target is met or modestly exceeded.

assumptions.name: Diluted share count, FY2028E
assumptions.rationale: FY2025 diluted weighted-average was 4,206m; total outstanding (Class A+B) 4,089m at Dec-2025, 4,079m at Jun-2026 (already declining on buybacks). Base assumes continued net share-count reduction from the $1.75bn cumulative buyback authorization roughly offsetting convertible-note dilution and stock-based compensation issuance. Bear assumes convertible-note dilution and continued SBC issuance dominate a slower buyback pace. Bull assumes an accelerated buyback given FCF generation.

assumptions.name: Target forward EV/Adjusted EBITDA multiple applied to FY2028E (for a 2028-based valuation cross-check)
assumptions.rationale: Base sits between Grab's current ~9.6x forward multiple and the peer average of Uber (~14.8x)/GoTo (~15.1x), reflecting partial but not full closure of the valuation gap identified in VAL-05 as fundamentals continue to be proven out. Bear assumes no re-rating and some further multiple compression on confirmed competitive erosion. Bull assumes convergence toward peer multiples on confirmed execution.

assumptions.name: Net cash / investment balance available for discounting back to present value (illustrative, not a full DCF)
assumptions.rationale: FY2025/Q2 2026 net cash liquidity of $5.4bn as the starting point; bear assumes continued Financial Services capital consumption and buyback spend draw this down over the forecast horizon; bull assumes strong Adjusted FCF generation (per A-09) more than offsets buybacks and Financial Services capital needs, growing net cash.

assumptions.name: Illustrative discount rate for present-valuing FY2028E scenario outcomes back to present
assumptions.rationale: Judgmental cost-of-equity proxy for a USD-reporting, ASEAN-EM-revenue, high-growth digital-platform business with a dual-class structure; not derived from a formal CAPM/WACC build in this pass (see research gap RG-03 on macro-data access). Bear/bull vary with perceived country/regulatory/competitive risk premium.

assumptions.name: Vietnam regulatory outcome -- commission/fare policy impact on Group revenue
assumptions.rationale: Base case assumes the National Competition Commission review (opened September 2026) concludes with disclosure/transparency requirements but no binding commission cap, a modest reputational/compliance cost. Bear assumes a mandated commission cap or fare-setting restriction in Vietnam that also invites similar scrutiny in 1-2 other ASEAN markets. Bull assumes the review is resolved with no material business changes.

assumptions.name: Grab-GoTo combination probability within 24 months
assumptions.rationale: Recurring, unconfirmed speculation since at least 2020, with a formal denial in June 2025 followed by renewed reports (including potential Danantara/Indonesian sovereign-fund involvement) through late 2025/2026. Base case treats this as a low-to-moderate probability, high-impact tail scenario rather than a base-case assumption; it is not incorporated into the base-case revenue/EBITDA forecasts above.
